name: Core Security
summary: The foundational toolkit: discovery, packet analysis, TLS checks and network utilities
description: A compact, broadly useful set of command-line and graphical tools for authorized security work: host and service discovery, a packet analyser, TLS checks, a password manager and the common network utilities the other profiles build on. Like every profile it is installed on demand; start here, the specialised profiles add to it.

tools.name: arp-scan
tools.summary: Discover and fingerprint IP hosts on the local network with ARP

tools.name: DNS lookup utilities
tools.summary: dig, delv and nslookup DNS query clients from BIND 9

tools.name: MASSCAN
tools.summary: Asynchronous TCP port scanner for large address ranges

tools.name: Nmap
tools.summary: Network exploration tool and security/port scanner

tools.name: traceroute
tools.summary: Trace the route IPv4/IPv6 packets take to a host

tools.name: whois
tools.summary: Query WHOIS registries for domain and network ownership

tools.name: Zenmap
tools.summary: Graphical front end for the Nmap scanner
tools.notes: Runs scans as your own user; privileged scan types still need root, which Zenmap asks for when you choose them.

tools.name: tcpdump
tools.summary: Command-line network packet capture and inspection

tools.name: Wireshark
tools.summary: Graphical network protocol analyser
tools.notes: Capturing needs permission to the interface; Debian's dpkg-reconfigure wireshark-common sets up the 'wireshark' group so you need not run it as root.

tools.name: age
tools.summary: Simple, modern file-encryption tool

tools.name: cryptsetup
tools.summary: Manage LUKS and dm-crypt encrypted volumes

tools.name: curl
tools.summary: Transfer data to or from a server over many protocols

tools.name: GnuPG
tools.summary: OpenPGP encryption and signing of files and email

tools.name: KeePassXC
tools.summary: Offline, encrypted password manager for engagement credentials
tools.notes: Transitional package; it pulls in keepassxc-full. Keep client and scope credentials out of shell history and in a vault like this one.

tools.name: Kleopatra
tools.summary: Graphical certificate and OpenPGP/S-MIME key manager

tools.name: secure-delete
tools.summary: Securely wipe files, free space, swap and memory

tools.name: socat

tools.name: Steghide

tools.name: WhatWeb

external.name: Metasploit Framework
external.summary: Widely used exploitation and payload development framework
external.license: BSD-3-Clause for the framework; the Rapid7 installer and some content have their own terms.

why.text: The framework is not packaged in Debian; Rapid7 ships its own cross-distribution installer and nightly builds and expects to be updated from there.

how.text: Install the official omnibus package or nightly build from Rapid7's documented instructions for Linux, then update with msfupdate.

external.name: VeraCrypt
external.summary: On-the-fly disk and volume encryption with hidden volumes
external.license: Apache-2.0 plus the TrueCrypt License 3.0; the latter is not DFSG-free, so VeraCrypt is not in Debian.

why.text: VeraCrypt carries the non-free TrueCrypt licence terms and is not in Debian; the project publishes its own installers and packages.

how.text: Download the official Debian/Ubuntu package or generic installer from the VeraCrypt site and install it; cryptsetup (in Debian) covers LUKS/dm-crypt natively.
